summary.headline: CL Educate revenue rose about 55% to ₹570 crore in FY26 and EBITDA more than doubled to ₹69 crore, driven by the DEXIT acquisition.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 as the first year the group crossed ₹500 crore revenue, with revenue up from ₹368 crore to ₹570 crore and EBITDA up from ₹33 crore to ₹69 crore. Cash generated from operations rose to ₹79 crore from ₹26 crore, and the acquisition-linked borrowing has been reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹180 crore. The DEXIT (assessments) integration is described as complete. The L&D/EdTech segment remains under structural pressure, with realisations down 12-14% and revenue down about 11%, and management expects it to stay flat for roughly four more quarters. Fundraising has been put on a slight pause.

financial_highlights.change: acquisition debt reduced to ₹180 crore from ₹210 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance (as on date)
financial_highlights.change: from about ₹50 crore last year, excluding ₹185-190 crore pending RPS redemption

segments.name: Assessments (DEXIT)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to ₹223 crore from ₹205 crore and EBITDA to about ₹51 crore from ₹34 crore. All existing contracts were rolled over and 20 new customers were added. FY27 order book is about 80-85% of FY26 revenue, per management.

segments.name: L&D / EdTech (test prep, university engagement, publishing)
segments.commentary: Enrollment volume grew about 4% but average realisation fell 12-14%, so revenue declined about 11%. Management expects revenue to stay roughly flat for about four quarters, with profitability improving from Q1 FY27 after cost recalibration.

segments.name: MarTech (Kestone, events, VOSMOS, VIRSA)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 11% to about ₹161 crore: international up about 20%, India up about 5%. EBITDA was slightly lower due to set-up costs for the new social events and luxury wedding business. Domestic to international mix is about 1:2.

guidance_outlook: Assessments: management expects reasonably healthy revenue growth in FY27, backed by an order book of about 80-85% of FY26 revenue six weeks into the year.
L&D: revenue expected flat for about four more quarters; profitability expected to show upward movement from Q1 FY27.
MarTech: shift to higher-margin CEP and VOSMOS/VIRSA products over 12-18 months; pruning low-margin MMS and pass-through businesses.
Discontinued operations: bulk of losses done, with a little residual impact possible in Q1 FY27 and none expected beyond that.
Talevate: target to sign 8-10 corporates and about 100 jobs over the next few quarters, testing the MVP before scaling.
capex_capacity: Working capital is about 50% of revenue despite about 50% revenue growth, per management.
Management is marketing land assets, including a Raipur plot earmarked for a school, and is seeking a buyer at the right price.
A new EdTech personalised-learning pilot is to launch in about one month, with a roll-out to all programmes and centres if successful.
Remote proctoring and BYOD technology is being built out at DEXIT; the mySathi IP platform has started going to market.
Settlement of ₹185-190 crore RPS amount awaits NCLT capital reduction approval; order reserved, next hearing on May 15, 2026.
demand_pricing: L&D: enrollment volume up about 4%, but realisation down 12-14%. Students are shifting from ₹30,000-60,000 full programmes to ₹2,000-4,000 modular components.
MBA revenue expected flat to slightly down, with volumes rising. UG segments (law, BBA, IPM) are holding or raising prices, and growth is expected there.
Assessments: government contracts are about 40-45% of mix and private 55-60%. Pricing is similar across both and the market is price-sensitive.
Assessments: rollover of exam dates by 60-120 days shifted some FY26 revenue into FY27.
Competition: PhysicsWallah-type players are seen as low-price and not a direct threat; management launched products at about 50% above PhysicsWallah pricing and one-third of regular prices.

qa_highlights.question: Does the NEET controversy open opportunities for DEXIT in nationwide exams?
qa_highlights.answer: Yatrik Vin said it is a significant opportunity; DEXIT already conducts exams for IRDAI, ICAI and NISM, and its digital and surveillance tech is ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DEXIT government/private mix, contract duration, and government tender criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Government is about 40-45% and private 55-60%. Contract tenure varies from one to five years, or order-based. RFPs weigh technical at 65-70% and commercial at 30-35%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the order book work, and why is it not 100% revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 80-85% coverage is in hand for FY27, and sales efforts target a higher rollover. Exam timing set by clients can push revenue into the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fundraising plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Satya Narayanan said fundraising is on a slight pause given the environment, and the boards want value at the right valuation. Updates are expected in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the cash and current liabilities linked to NSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹182 crore was left behind from the NSEIT transition and has earned ₹11-12 crore of interest, so about ₹193-194 crore is on the balance sheet. It will be knocked off against RPS after NCLT approval and moved from non-current to current liabilities.

qa_highlights.question: How will VIRSA affect MarTech in North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilots with Salesforce, Dell and Infosys have had positive feedback. The Salesforce work is for Canada, with a scale-up to the US expected over the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: L&D revenue flat for about four quarters, with AI and modular pricing pressure expected to persist for four to five quarters.
Assessment revenue timing depends on client exam schedules, which have rolled over by 60-120 days before.
Pending NCLT approval for the capital reduction and ₹185-190 crore RPS redemption; timing of upstreaming to NSE Investments is 'hopefully over this year'.
Fundraising is on pause, with no timeline given.
Interest and depreciation of ₹85 crore weighs on profitability; PPA-related depreciation is included.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the DEXIT/assessments and group scale narrative, with emphasis on the integration and cash generation. Cautious and somewhat hedged on EdTech, which management says will stay flat in revenue, and deliberately non-committal on timing for fundraising, the NCLT capital reduction and new initiatives.
key_quotes: This was the first year when CL as a group crossed the ₹ 500 crore revenue threshold.

So despite the fact that our volume of enrollment grew by about 4%, the average realization saw a dramatic downward movement of about 12 to 14%, which resulted in our overall revenue declining by about 11% from the previous year.

adds.what: New EdTech personalised-learning pilot (not a physical capacity; roll-out to all programmes and centres if successful)

growth.why: Assessments order book for FY27 is about 80-85% of FY26 revenue (₹223 crore base), supporting management's guidance of reasonably healthy FY27 growth, while L&D revenue is guided flat for about four quarters with EdTech profitability improving from Q1 FY27; MarTech grew about 11% with no numeric forward guide.
